I am an old man now, 58 years, and I have farmed these lands all my life here in Tabora. This plot is not mine — I rent it — so I will not waste money putting expensive fertilizer on another man's land, especially for beans. Beans do not need much fertilizer anyway, my father taught me they feed the soil themselves. I will plant the seeds I saved from last harvest, together with maize between the rows as we always do. The rains come once here, so I must wait for God and work with my hoe. If my back troubles me too much at weeding time, I will call one or two young men from the village to help me for a few days.
